data.description:
## Symptom

`tests/external/test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py::test_anthropic_auth_oracle_isolated_from_provider_import_order[test_empty_anthropic_carrier_fails_closed]`
failed once inside a full `pytest tests/unit tests/scripts` run (16,717 other tests passed), and
**passes when run standalone** (4 passed).

Observed 2026-09-04 during unrelated work on bug `9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`. `tests/e2e` was not even
collected in the failing run, and the change under test touched only e2e provisioning, so the
change could not have participated.

## Why this is filed as a candidate rather than a confirmed defect

The evidence is a **single observation**. What it does establish:

- It is **order-dependent**, not deterministic: standalone passes, full-suite fails.
- The suite runs under random ordering, so the triggering order is not yet known.
- The test's own subject is **provider import ordering** and lazy-import isolation, which is exactly
  the kind of global state (module import cache, environment carriers) that leaks between tests.

What it does NOT establish: the direction of the leak. It is unknown whether the test under
inspection is polluted by an earlier test, or whether the test is itself insufficiently isolated and
merely gets away with it in most orders. Those have different fixes, and guessing between them is
how a flake gets papered over.

## Why it matters, per project policy

AGENTS.md is explicit: *"A flaky test is a BUG to root-cause, never a retry. A test that fails
intermittently gets debugged — reproduce it deterministically... and fix the class, not the one run.
Retrying until green slows development, wastes tokens, and erodes CI as a regression oracle."*

A held-out isolation oracle that is itself order-sensitive is a particularly bad case: its whole
purpose is to prove isolation, so when it fails for isolation reasons the signal is ambiguous
precisely where it needs to be sharp.

## Acceptance criteria

All deterministic and verifiable in a single run — no "observe over N days".

1. The failure is **reproduced deterministically**: a specific seed or an explicit test ordering
   (`-p no:randomly` with a named order, or `pytest -p randomly --randomly-seed=<N>`) that fails
   every time it is run. Record the exact command. Until this exists the bug is not understood, and
   no fix should be attempted.
2. The **direction of the leak** is established with evidence: either an earlier test mutates shared
   state the oracle depends on (name it), or the oracle depends on ambient state it does not
   establish for itself (name it). State which, and quote what proves it.
3. Fixed at the **class** level, not by pinning this one test's order. Ordering pins mask the leak
   and leave every sibling exposed.
4. Post-fix, the reproduction from AC1 passes, and the test still passes standalone and in a full
   run.
5. **Defect-seeded**: reintroducing the leak identified in AC2 makes the AC1 reproduction fail again,
   demonstrated by mutation and then reverted. A guard that stays green under mutation proves nothing.

## Note

If investigation shows this is not reproducible under any ordering, close it as not-reproducible with
the seeds tried recorded — that is a legitimate outcome and worth writing down, since the next
observer should not start from zero.
data.title: Order-dependent failure in test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout: passes standalone, fails in a full suite run under random ordering
